concept.name: OHLCV bar
concept.definition: An OHLCV bar is an OHLC bar augmented with the total trading volume over the same interval. It is the standard record layout for aggregated market data; in finance literature the OHLCV data is sometimes called 'candles'.
concept.intuition: OHLCV adds 'how much traded' to the four price extremes, so each record captures both the price path summary and the activity level behind it.
concept.mechanics: For each aggregation interval, compute open/high/low/close from the trade sequence and sum traded quantities into V; many feeds add quote-asset volume and trade count alongside. Daily, weekly, monthly, and intraday equity series from vendors such as Alpha Vantage are delivered in this layout.
concept.formula: O = p_first; H = max(p_i); L = min(p_i); C = p_last; V = Σ q_i, over trades i in the interval.
concept.failure_modes: Volume conventions differ across vendors (consolidated vs single-venue, inclusion of auction volume and off-exchange prints), so the V field is not always comparable across sources. The bar still hides intra-period sequencing.
concept.misconceptions: OHLCV bars are not raw market data — they are an aggregation; assuming they preserve tick-level information leads to unrealistic backtest fills.
concept.example: A 5-minute AAPL bar of O=189.10, H=189.45, L=189.00, C=189.30, V=412,000 summarizes all trades in that five-minute window.
